reasons.plausibility: Introducing 10-20 vol% pores will inevitably reduce strength, especially at 1000°C, because pores act as stress concentrators and reduce load-bearing area; the claim that strength is maintained contradicts well-established structure-property relationships for porous metals.
reasons.testability: The test is clearly defined with specific measurements and a quantitative falsification criterion, though the sintering conditions (900°C, 20 MPa) are unusual for this refractory alloy and may not achieve the stated porosity.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis is not useful because it proposes a physically unsound mechanism (pores maintaining strength) and would misdirect research effort away from viable density-reduction strategies like alloying with lighter elements.
